page.overview:
What is Felaróf?

Felaróf was a white horse and the first of the Mearas, known for being exceptionally fast. It was said that Felaróf could understand the speech of Men.

Felaróf was a wild foal when he was captured by the horse tamer Léod, father of Eorl the Young, who attempted to tame the white colt despite no one being able to tame it. However, when he attempted to ride the horse, it threw him, resulting in the tamer's death. His orphaned son Eorl hunted down the horse, but instead of killing it, he demanded that it serve him as payment for causing his father's death. The horse accepted this, taking the name Felaróf.

Eorl rode Felaróf without bit or bridle. When he came to the aid of Gondor, the victory which led Steward Cirion to grant the Éothéod the land of Calenardhon, which would become Rohan. Thirty years later, horse and rider met their end fighting the Easterlings in the Wold of Rohan and were buried together in a mound raised outside the gate of Edoras.

His line, the Mearas, according to tradition could only be ridden by the Lord of the Mark. Gandalf's horse Shadowfax came from the Mearas, making him a descendant of Felaróf himself.
